title: How to design an app SO addictive people cant stop using it
additional_url_type: YouTube guide to viewing a transcript
what_it_supports: Six stages, descriptions, chapter offsets, and spoken claims.
limitations: A design teardown, not an experimental study. Caption text not independently checked against audio.

title: YAZIO's Black Hat Paywall Trick (App Breakdown #60)
what_it_supports: March 18 walkthrough of the specific Yazio version, onboarding, friction and AI camera. Companion page gives chapter links and screen examples.
limitations: A first-look teardown; not proof of current behavior everywhere or of a retention effect.

title: Finch: The Self-Care App That's Actually Addictive (App Breakdown #55)
what_it_supports: March 11 walkthrough of goal completion, pet energy, adventures, contextual permission and widget pitch.
limitations: An on-screen 4× widget claim has no linked methods or corroborating report; not a causal or clinical study.

title: Hooked: How to Build Habit-Forming Products
author_or_organization: Nir Eyal; edited by Ryan Hoover
what_it_supports: Trigger, action, variable reward, and investment; internal and external cues.
limitations: Practitioner framework, not evidence that all six stages work together or raise retention.

title: How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world
author_or_organization: Phillippa Lally; Cornelia H. M. van Jaarsveld; Henry W. W. Potts; Jane Wardle
what_it_supports: In a 39-person well-fit subset, median 66 modeled days to 95% of personal automaticity plateau; range 18–254. One miss was not materially disruptive in this study.
limitations: Daily health-behavior volunteers and model estimates; not a universal number of days or app interactions.

title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes
what_it_supports: Linking a chosen goal action to a concrete future situation can aid goal pursuit.
limitations: Goal achievement is not equivalent to notification conversion or app retention.

title: The attentional cost of receiving a cell phone notification
author_or_organization: Cary Stothart; Ainsley Mitchum; Courtney Yehnert
what_it_supports: Notifications can affect attention-task performance without a tap.
limitations: Lab calls and texts; not a field estimate for every push.

title: A behavior model for persuasive design
relation_to_video: Matched to named scholar and model
what_it_supports: Motivation, ability and a trigger/prompt together; useful checklist for designing an action.
limitations: Conceptual model; B=MAP is not a quantitative formula or lift estimate.

title: The information capacity of the human motor system in controlling the amplitude of movement
what_it_supports: Movement time depends on target distance and width in aimed movement.
limitations: Does not specify an ideal CTA location or a universal mobile thumb zone.

title: Do Defaults Save Lives?
author_or_organization: Eric J. Johnson; Daniel G. Goldstein
source_type: Science Policy Forum, experiment and observational analyses
what_it_supports: Hypothetical consent differs by default; separately describes country consent and actual donations.
limitations: 42/82/79% are hypothetical; country consent does not equal transplants or identify a causal magnitude.

title: Impact of presumed consent for organ donation on donation rates: a systematic review
author_or_organization: Amber Rithalia; Catriona McDaid; Sara Suekarran; Lindsey Myers; Amanda Sowden
additional_url_type: Executive summary of related longer NIHR review
what_it_supports: Presumed consent was associated with donation rates in reviewed settings; multiple influences matter.
limitations: Observational and before–after designs cannot cleanly isolate the law's effect.

title: When and why defaults influence decisions: a meta-analysis of default effects
author_or_organization: Jon M. Jachimowicz; Shannon Duncan; Elke U. Weber; Eric J. Johnson
what_it_supports: Preselection often influences choice; effect sizes vary and depend on design and setting.
limitations: Choice uptake is not welfare, user satisfaction, or outcome attainment.

title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
author_or_organization: Benjamin Scheibehenne; Rainer Greifeneder; Peter M. Todd
what_it_supports: Average choice-overload effect near zero in this synthesis; variation matters.
limitations: Does not imply menus are always useful or that option structure does not matter.

title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
author_or_organization: Alexander Chernev; Ulf Böckenholt; Joseph Goodman
additional_url_type: Author-hosted full PDF (check the publisher corrigendum)
what_it_supports: Identifies moderators: complexity, difficulty, preference uncertainty, goals.
limitations: Not a universal maximum number of choices; corrected coefficients are not used in the guide.

title: Schedules of Reinforcement
author_or_organization: Charles B. Ferster; B. F. Skinner
what_it_supports: Documents laboratory reinforcement schedules and different response patterns.
limitations: Animal behavior and experimental conditions; not the exact two-group protocol as told.

title: Partial reinforcement: a review and critique
author_or_organization: William O. Jenkins; Julian C. Stanley Jr.
what_it_supports: Reviews persistence under extinction following continuous vs. partial reinforcement.
limitations: Early review; does not establish usefulness or addiction in mobile app users.

title: Key pecking during extinction after intermittent or continuous reinforcement as a function of the number of reinforcers delivered during training
author_or_organization: T. J. Zarcone; M. N. Branch; C. E. Hughes; H. S. Pennypacker
additional_url_type: PubMed Central abstract and full PDF link
what_it_supports: Within-subject test in seven pigeons; generally more extinction responses in the former variable-ratio component.
limitations: Not a replication of the narration's alleged two-group protocol; not human UX evidence.

title: 'Superstition' in the pigeon
additional_url_type: B. F. Skinner Foundation full reprint PDF
what_it_supports: Food delivered independent of behavior; often conflated with operant schedule studies in coverage.
limitations: Skinner's interpretation has been challenged; this is not the narrated study.

title: The superstition experiment: A reexamination of its implications for the principles of adaptive behavior
author_or_organization: John E. R. Staddon; Virginia L. Simmelhag
what_it_supports: Reexamines why behavior occurs under periodic response-independent food delivery.
limitations: Mechanistic disagreement is not a finding about people using dating apps.

title: A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation
author_or_organization: Edward L. Deci; Richard Koestner; Richard M. Ryan
what_it_supports: Some expected, contingent rewards reduced free-choice engagement; positive feedback sometimes helped.
limitations: Effects differ by type and context; not a claim that badges always harm or all feedback helps.

title: The Gamification of Learning: a Meta-analysis
what_it_supports: Small positive average learning effects, with results varying by outcome and methods.
limitations: Educational gamification is not evidence for a slot machine mechanic or all types of apps.

title: The Loop and Reasons to Break It: Investigating Infinite Scrolling Behaviour in Social Media Applications and Reasons to Stop
what_it_supports: One-week study of scrolling and why users stopped; distinguishes within-session and repeated-use loops.
limitations: Small observational study; no random assignment to infinite vs. paginated feed.

title: An Experimental Study Of Netflix Use and the Effects of Autoplay on Watching Behaviors
what_it_supports: Disabling Netflix autoplay produced shorter viewing sessions and less daily viewing relative to control.
limitations: US study with 76 users; a consumption effect, not a clinical or long-term retention finding.

title: 101 reasons to stop: A systematic review of media cues for disengagement
what_it_supports: Catalogs cues to stop across devices, apps, features, interactions and messages.
limitations: Small and varied literature; not a pooled effect for infinite scrolling.

title: The Netflix Recommender System: Algorithms, Business Value, and Innovation
what_it_supports: Section 3 estimates more than $1B/year for recommendations and personalization combined; section 4 explains experiments.
limitations: Historical Netflix estimate, not an audited figure or a causal estimate for a single algorithm or history feature.

title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence
what_it_supports: Across 138 randomized studies (N=19,951), monitoring-promoting interventions improved goal attainment (d=0.40, 95% CI 0.32–0.48).
limitations: Does not recommend public tracking, punishment, or substituting an app streak for an actual goal.

title: The Endowed Progress Effect: How Artificial Advancement Increases Effort
what_it_supports: Progress framing affected persistence and completion, including in a loyalty setting.
limitations: Not evidence to fake a streak or advance a progress bar without a genuine action.

title: Consumer switching costs: A typology, antecedents, and consequences
author_or_organization: Thomas A. Burnham; Judy K. Frels; Vijay Mahajan
what_it_supports: Distinguishes procedural, financial, and relational costs of switching.
limitations: Stated intentions and switching costs are not the same as user value; not grounds for lock-in.

title: Controlled experiments on the web: survey and practical guide
author_or_organization: Ron Kohavi; Roger Longbotham; Dan Sommerfield; Randal M. Henne
what_it_supports: Randomization, interpretation, power, and engineering of trustworthy tests.
limitations: A method, not product-specific evidence of retention lift.

title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments: A Taxonomy and Rules of Thumb for Practitioners
what_it_supports: An unexpected treatment/control split can signal implementation or data quality problems.
limitations: Passing a sample-ratio check does not prove an experiment is otherwise valid.

title: On or Off Track: How (Broken) Streaks Affect Consumer Decisions
what_it_supports: Logged streak framing can affect subsequent engagement; making a break repairable attenuated the effect.
limitations: Does not establish a universal streak strategy or justify fabricating progress or selling recovery.

title: On the rate of gain of information
additional_url_type: Abstract of 2018 review by Proctor and Schneider
what_it_supports: Choice reaction time varies with uncertainty in a controlled task.
limitations: Not a maximum menu size or evidence to hide needed choices.

title: Purpose Mode: Reducing Distraction through Toggling Attention Capture Damaging Patterns on Social Media Web Sites
author_or_organization: Hao-Ping (Hank) Lee; Yi-Shyuan Chiang; Lan Gao; Stephanie Yang; Philipp Winter; Sauvik Das
what_it_supports: Users reported less distraction during a second week in which they could turn off interface features.
limitations: Small before–after design; bundled switches and no parallel control to isolate a feature.

title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
author_or_organization: Nicholas J. Cepeda; Harold Pashler; Edward Vul; John T. Wixted; Doug Rohrer
what_it_supports: Distributed practice and the planned delay to recall jointly influence memory performance.
limitations: Retention of learned material is not app retention. Does not test Duolingo’s product.

title: App Annie Mobile App Evolution (reported in TechCrunch)
author_or_organization: App Annie; reporting by Sarah Perez
additional_url_type: Original App Annie URL; redirected and failed to load at review
what_it_supports: Historical estimate of 93 installed and 41 used monthly in 2019.
limitations: Facebook-commissioned industry data, not a current universal average.

title: How Do Users Really Hold Mobile Devices?
what_it_supports: 49% of active-touch observations used a one-handed grip, in this sample.
limitations: Not 49% of all user sessions or all current users. No device or demographic breakdown.

title: Improving the streak: Forming habits one lesson at a time
what_it_supports: One lesson rather than the full daily goal; Day-14 retention +3.3% relative; daily goal completion decreased.
limitations: Company-specific, no public confidence interval here, doesn't measure learning gains.

title: Cal AI’s Zach Yadegari on how to create viral growth and capitalize on it
what_it_supports: Reports more than 15M downloads in less than two years.
limitations: Downloads are not unique active users, retention, or proof of causation.

title: How can I record food from restaurants or canteens?
additional_url_type: Linked official guide to saved meals
what_it_supports: Yazio also supports photo estimates that can be reviewed and edited.
limitations: Availability and entry flows may vary by time, market, platform, and plan.

title: Introducing the new Duolingo learning path
additional_url_type: Linked official guide to spacing and course practice
what_it_supports: Guided next lesson with built-in practice and some alternatives.
limitations: Documents a design, not evidence for its causal impact in another app.

title: TikTok executives know about app’s effect on teens, lawsuit documents allege
what_it_supports: Reports on previously public excerpts citing internal material; gives context and TikTok response.
limitations: Not the underlying study or a clinical threshold; complaint material was sealed, and TikTok disputed characterization.

title: Attorney General Coleman Sues TikTok for Addictive Harm to Kentucky Youth
author_or_organization: Kentucky Office of the Attorney General
what_it_supports: Confirms filing and describes state's allegations.
limitations: A litigant's announcement, not a judgment or proof of claims.

title: Recode Decode interview on Swiped: Hooking Up in the Digital Age
author_or_organization: Nancy Jo Sales interviewed by Recode
what_it_supports: Recounts Jonathan Badeen's Skinner inspiration and slot-machine analogy.
limitations: Design-origin recollection, not a controlled clinical study or a reliable summary of the animal protocol.

title: Aza Raskin on why technology – and democracy – are in an imagination crisis
author_or_organization: Aza Raskin with Adam Grant / TED ReThinking
relation_to_video: Matched to named estimate; not the only telling
what_it_supports: Raskin recounts his infinite-scroll invention and estimates aggregate time in human lifetimes.

title: How to autoplay the next episode
what_it_supports: Netflix has per-profile autoplay controls.
limitations: Does not estimate an effect on viewing or welfare.

title: How Netflix’s Recommendations System Works
what_it_supports: Explains how explicit and implicit signals shape recommendations.
limitations: Company overview, not an independent algorithm audit.

title: For You
what_it_supports: Explains the personalized feed, reasons and controls, including refresh.
limitations: Company description; does not prove claims about addiction or the effects of individual signals.

title: Explore

what_it_supports: Documents the swipe and match pattern in Explore and Discovery.

title: MyFitnessPal expands its position in digital nutrition tracking with Cal AI acquisition
what_it_supports: Confirms acquisition and describes the AI-first product positioning.
limitations: Does not validate the acquisition rationale as causal evidence or supply an independent downloads audit.

title: Finch official site
what_it_supports: Self-care routine plus pet care product framing.
limitations: Product marketing, not evidence of health outcomes or retention effects.

title: Requesting a copy of your personal data
what_it_supports: Example of a data request and machine-readable format.

title: What are meals?

limitations: Not a research source.

what_it_supports: Original link from main video's description.

title: José Gonçalves on X
what_it_supports: Original link from main video's description.
limitations: Not a research source.

title: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum)
what_it_supports: Minimum target size or allowed exceptions, plus an enhanced target size for web inputs.
limitations: CSS pixels are distinct from iOS points and Android dp; this is one criterion, not full conformance.

title: Accessibility, Human Interface Guidelines
what_it_supports: Controls, labels, adequate sizing and alternatives. iOS/iPadOS 44 × 44 pt default control size in the HIG table.
limitations: Apply to the relevant platform; test beyond compliance checklists.

title: Compose accessibility API defaults
what_it_supports: 48 dp Material touch target and techniques for accessible Compose controls.
limitations: Native Android conventions; not a web CSS requirement.

title: Asking permission to use notifications
what_it_supports: Request explicit authorization in context; users can change settings.
limitations: OS authorization does not replace an app-level preference or other privacy obligations.

title: Notification runtime permission
what_it_supports: Platform permission, request timing and handling denial.
limitations: Behavior varies by OS and target SDK; test on supported versions.

title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
what_it_supports: Design review reference for friction, hidden terms, and deception that undermines choice.
limitations: Staff report, not a standalone rule or jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

title: Guidelines 03/2022 on Deceptive Design Patterns in Social Media Platform Interfaces (v2.0)
what_it_supports: Examples of deceptive consent/closing flows, transparency, and data minimization.
limitations: Addresses GDPR in the social-media setting; check applicability and current obligations before launch.

title: Guidelines on the protection of minors under the DSA
what_it_supports: Recommends safer defaults and reducing features such as autoplay and push that contribute to excessive use for minors.
limitations: Context is online platforms in scope of the DSA; obtain separate review for the release markets and users.

title: Recommendation systems overview
what_it_supports: Candidate generation, scoring, and re-ranking architecture.
limitations: A design pattern, not a requirement to use ML for an MVP.
